exposure: induction of labor between 41(+2) and 41(+6) weeks

Implementation of new Danish guidelines for post-date pregnancies (induction of labor between 41+2 and 41+6 weeks, earlier induction at 41+0 weeks for maternal age >40 years or BMI >35 kg/m2, and fetal surveillance at 41+0 weeks)
Years before (2008-2010) vs. after (2012-2014) new national guidelines
induction of labor at gestational age (GA) of 42(+0) weeks
earlier induction at 41(+0) weeks in the case of maternal age >40 years or body mass index (BMI) >35 kg/m(2)
outcome: Apgar score below 7 at five minutes
cohort: All pregnancies in Denmark that reached 41+0 weeks of gestation in 2008-2014 (n = 102,167)
finding: Implementation of new Danish guidelines for post-date pregnancies was associated with a decline in stillbirths and perinatal mortality, while the rates of cesarean section and vacuum extraction remained stable despite an increase in labor inductions.
mod_finding: The risk of vacuum extraction decreased after the implementation of new Danish guidelines for post-date pregnancies, while the risk of cesarean section remained stable despite an increase in labor inductions.
